item.title: Jensen Huang's third affair with Nvidia employee emerges after exit
item.description: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. Reuters is not naming the second employee.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. ALSO READ: Trump says ex Apple CEO Cook is 'a legend', should replace Huang at Nvidia Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were not successful. Nvidia declined to comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia's board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment. ALSO READ: Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO amid affair, spy allegations: What we know  Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.  ALSO READ: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit jolts tech world, raises AI concerns The former Nvidia CEO's decision to resign from the company could disrupt the AI industry that he helped shape. Nvidia has used its financial strength to help create an industry around AI through complex financial arrangements that ease the purchase of the company's chips. It has backed cloud computing companies and AI labs in order to do so. Pressure on Jensen Huang, who is 63 and married, to resign mounted after reports of his affair with Alice Huang. Nvidia's board appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search to replace Jensen Huang. The board is considering internal and external candidates for the job. Earlier this month, Nvidia's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. Shares fell 5.5% on Thursday in active trading. The stock has shed more than 30% of its value since its early October peak.

item.title: US lawmakers push for tougher curbs on advanced AI chip exports to China
item.description: US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Huang ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / US lawmakers push for tougher curbs on advanced AI chip exports to China

US lawmakers push for tougher curbs on advanced AI chip exports to China US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Huang

The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 1:30 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Chinese AI shares tumbled on Friday, as investors worried that Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO could further restrict Chinese access to advanced US chips, deepening the technology divide between the world's two biggest economies.   US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Huang, who has pushed to preserve access to the Chinese market and has close ties with US President Donald Trump.   Huang stepped down after news reports of a romantic relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development.   Senior White House officials were also discussing whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation said, as the desire to take action rose across Washington. Also Read

Alice Huang had stake in China data centre serving Huawei, says report

From gaming chips to AI dominance: How Nvidia became a tech powerhouse

Fallout from Nvidia scandal may dampen investor exuberance around AI boom

US lawmakers step up pressure on Howard Lutnick as Nvidia row deepens

Meet Colette Kress, Nvidia's interim CEO after Jensen Huang's exit

A growing number of lawmakers have criticized Lutnick for the administration's refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a US trade blacklist, and questioned whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia's exports to China.   Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China's access to Nvidia's chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

"The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here," Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favored limiting China's access to the advanced technology. "I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take."   Investors dumped shares in Chinese AI models and hardware suppliers to the US on Friday, with AI model stocks Z.AI and MiniMax Group tumbling 12% and 8.4% respectively.   Data center suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink Technology, whose businesses are heavily reliant on US markets, also slumped more than 8%.   The Chinese businesswoman at the center of the scandal, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

REPUBLICANS EYE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS   The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions.   Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company's chips remotely.   Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defense  authorization bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday. The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling.   The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centers to access Nvidia chips.  SCRUTINY OF HUANG LIKELY TO CONTINUE   Huang's resignation is unlikely to end congressional scrutiny of Nvidia and could leave the former chief executive more exposed to investigation, said Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation.

"Congress can still subpoena him and Nvidia should conduct an independent investigation to determine whether the problems extend beyond Huang," Cheung said.   Cheung said Huang's departure could weaken Nvidia's influence in Washington and create additional momentum for legislation that tightens restrictions on advanced chip exports. He said Nvidia's new leadership could also reconsider the company's China strategy as it seeks to rebuild trust with US policymakers.   Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.

Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with Alice Huang.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Five things to know about APEC as Trump, Putin and Xi set to attend summit

Five things to know about APEC as Trump, Putin and Xi set to attend summit Founded as an informal 12-member dialogue effort in 1989 in the Australian capital Canberra, it has become the region's premier economic forum to foster ties on advancing growth, trade and investment

A worker pushes a row of trolleys past a promotion board for the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' meeting at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, in Shenzhen, China | Image: Reuters

Reuters HONG KONG 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 12:36 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Attention will focus next week on a summit of US, Chinese and Russian leaders set for the 21-member gathering of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China's southern technology hub of Shenzhen.   WHAT IS APEC?         Founded as an informal 12-member dialogue effort in 1989 in the Australian capital of Canberra, it has become the region's premier economic forum to foster ties on advancing growth, trade and investment.   Accounting for about 62% of global GDP and roughly half of global trade, the grouping of "member economies" rather than nations allows participation by Chinese-ruled Hong Kong and democratically governed Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its own territory.

It does not include India, the world's most populous nation, however. Also Read

Foreign businesses seized by Putin help fund Russia's war machine

Trump backed Huang despite spy allegations, urged him to fight for his job

Trump says ex Apple CEO Cook is 'a legend', should replace Huang at Nvidia

US returns over $12 bn in oil proceeds to Venezuela since Maduro's ouster

Trump says US doesn't need Iran deal, asks Vance to tackle corruption

APEC operates on non-binding commitments reached strictly by consensus, with commitments undertaken on a voluntary basis.   The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is set for November 18 and 19, preceded by an annual summit of CEOs on November 17-18.   WHY SHENZHEN?     China is hosting the summit for the third time, after events in the commercial hub of Shanghai in 2001 and the capital, Beijing, in 2014.   Both domestic and international reasons govern the choice of Shenzhen, adjacent to the financial centre of Hong Kong, said Chim Lee, senior analyst at the Economist Intelligence Unit.   As part of China's Greater Bay Area home to Hong Kong and Macau, which Beijing seeks to establish as a global hub for technology and innovation, the city offers a platform to showcase China's vision for development and trade.

It also highlights Shenzhen's resilience to geopolitical turbulence, Lee added.   The city is the base of several leading Chinese auto and tech giants, such as BYD, Huawei and Tencent .   WHO WILL BE THERE?     China has said President Xi Jinping will chair the leaders' meeting and deliver remarks. US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. are among those expected.   The leaders of Canada, Australia, Mexico and Indonesia are also due to attend, along with those of Malaysia, South Korea and Vietnam among Asia-Pacific nations.   Taiwan has designated Stan Shih, founder of Acer, as its envoy.   Tokyo has not formally said whether Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will attend and New Zealand has not officially confirmed its delegation.

WHAT TO WATCH AND KEY STICKING POINTS     West Asia Instability: The economic ripple effects of conflict, such as risks to energy security, trade flows, supply chains and inflation are major concerns expected to figure in talks.   Tripartite Dynamics: All eyes are on the possible meeting of Chinese, Russian and US leaders. China is hesitant to engage in talks on nuclear disarmament, as it has fewer such weapons than the other two, analysts said.   The US and Russia will also be keen to discuss the Ukraine war, but not necessarily China, they said.   China-US Relations: A key focus to see if ties can stay stable. Both sides are falling short on commitments to an extended trade truce, analysts said. Rare earth supplies, artificial intelligence and tariffs are also likely to figure on the agenda, with US arms sales to Taiwan closely watched.

China's ties with Japan and the Philippines: Strains in Japan and China ties have persisted since Prime Minister Takaichi angered Beijing in November 2025 by suggesting that Japan could deploy its military if a Chinese move against neighbouring Taiwan also threatened its territory.   China-Philippines relations will likewise be closely watched amid continuing tension in the disputed waterway of the South China Sea.   WHO ARE APEC'S MEMBERS?     These are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Peru, the Philippines, Russia, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, the United States and Vietnam.

item.description: SpiceJet's share of India's domestic aviation market, the world's third-largest, has plunged to just 0.6% from nearly 15% in 2019 ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / SpiceJet to file overdue financial results after BSE warns of suspension

SpiceJet to file overdue financial results after BSE warns of suspension SpiceJet's share of India's domestic aviation market, the world's third-largest, has plunged to just 0.6% from nearly 15% in 2019

The suspension will not take effect if SpiceJet complies with listing rules to the exchange's satisfaction by December 7, the notice said (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters NEW DELHI 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 12:35 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's SpiceJet said on Friday it will announce its overdue financial results by a December 7 deadline, days after one of the country's two main bourses warned it would suspend trading in shares of the cash-strapped airline if it failed to do so.   SpiceJet's share of India's domestic aviation market, the world's third-largest, has plunged to just 0.6% from nearly 15% in 2019. The airline has slashed flights, grounded planes and delayed salary payments to many of its pilots amid a cash crunch that has forced it to seek government-backed financing.   In a notice on Monday, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) in Mumbai said it would suspend trading in SpiceJet shares from December 10 because the airline had not filed its results for the March and June quarters.

The suspension will not take effect if SpiceJet complies with listing rules to the exchange's satisfaction by December 7, the notice said.   "The completion of audit has taken longer time and hence caused delay in filing of results," a SpiceJet spokesperson told Reuters, without explaining what delayed the audit. Also Read

Recovery signals: Sensex valuation rebounds as November rally gathers pace premium

The airline also said it had obtained an extension from the Registrar of Companies to hold its annual shareholder meeting for the financial year ended March 2026 by December 31. Under Indian law, companies must present their audited annual financial statements at such meetings.   BSE said that during any suspension, the shares held by SpiceJet's controlling shareholders, along with other securities in their electronic securities accounts, would be frozen.

SpiceJet's chairman and managing director, Ajay Singh, is among the airline's controlling shareholders. He did not immediately respond to a request for comment.   Singh personally held a 12% stake as of March 31, while the wider group of controlling shareholders owned 24.2%, according to the company's latest available shareholding disclosure.   SpiceJet competes with IndiGo and the Air India group, which together accounted for more than 90% of India's domestic passenger market in September. Its financial troubles have been worsened by the Middle East conflict, which has pushed up fuel prices and restricted airspace access.   SpiceJet last reported financial results in February, posting a consolidated net loss of 2.62 billion rupees ($27.8 million) for the October-December 2025 quarter.

Indian listing rules require companies to report quarterly results within 45 days of the end of each quarter, except the final quarter of the financial year, and audited annual results within 60 days of the financial year's end.   Separately, SpiceJet said on Friday its board would meet on November 18 to consider raising fresh capital through the issuance of shares, debt securities or other financial instruments.
